newsitem.title: USA: Judge rules Miami airport fees unfair.
newsitem.headline: Judge rules Miami airport fees unfair.

text.p: A group of airlines suing Miami International Airport won a battle in their lawsuit Tuesday when a judge decided some of MIA's fees are unfair.
"The judge has found it unfair to force the other airlines to pay for a facility they won't be entitled to use," United Airlines spokesman Richard Martin said.
Six airlines last year sued Dade County, which operates Miami International Airport, alleging that recent increases in landing and other fees and rents were unfair.
They maintained they were being asked to foot the bill for a fancy new terminal for the exclusive use of American Airlines, a unit of AMR Corp.
In a 101-page decision handed down Tuesday, Washington, D.C., Administrative Law Judge Ronnie Yoder ruled the "fees and charges are unfair and unreasonable by an undetermined amount."
He said the new terminal was "incomparable to the facilities provided or to be provided to the joint carriers."
Since only American will use the new terminal, the judge found the fees resulted in "discriminatory treatment of the other carriers."
U.S. Department of Transportation still must review the findings and make a final decision by March 19.
The six airlines are Air Canada, Delta Air Lines Inc, Deutsche Lufthansa AG, Trans World Airlines, UAL Corp unit United Airlines and USAir Group Inc.
The Florida judge who initially heard the suit decided she could not determine the reasonableness of the fees and referred that part of the suit to the U.S. Department of Transportation.
American Airlines and DOT did not immediately return calls for comment on Yoder's decision. Miami International Airport had no immediate comment.
